messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Single Cell Data Analysis 2.0 - Single-cell epidemiology methods
messages.subject_clean: Single Cell Data Analysis 2.0 - Single-cell epidemiology methods
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

Cell-level evidence can add resolution to population health questions. Single Cell Data Analysis 2.0 led by Nikolay Oskolkov (Lund University) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Process single-cell RNA sequencing data through quality control, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and differential expression analysis. Use R and Python tools, including Seurat and Scanpy, to integrate datasets and investigate cellular heterogeneity in epidemiological research. Connect computational results to biological inference while accounting for batch effects and data structure.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/single-cell-data-analysis-20-1
The full course outline is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Longitudinal Biostatistics Methods in R
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

Repeated observations require attention to correlation, missingness, and clustered study structures. Longitudinal Analysis in Biostatistics led by Md Tuhin Sheikh (Biostatistics, College of Health Solutions, Arizona State University) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Marginal and conditional models, correlation structures, and multilevel methods support analysis of repeated epidemiological observations. Participants use R and RStudio to address missingness patterns, multiple imputation, sensitivity analysis, and fixed and random effects. Epidemiologists can apply these approaches to cohort, patient, and clustered data when estimating change over time.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/longitudinal-analysis-in-biostatistics
The full course outline is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Cell and Gene Therapy: Design, Estimands, Operations, and AI - livestream seminar
messages.subject_clean: Cell and Gene Therapy: Design, Estimands, Operations, and AI - livestream seminar
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone

Instats is excited to offer a 1-day seminar, Cell and Gene Therapy: Design, Estimands, Operations, and AI <https://instats.org/seminar/cell-and-gene-therapy-design-estimands-o>, livestreaming October 6 and sponsored by the American Statistical Association?s Cell and Gene Therapy Scientific Working Group. As cell and gene therapies rapidly reshape biomedical innovation, this seminar provides PhD students, academic researchers, and applied scientists with a coherent framework for evaluating complex interventions across translational research, clinical development, and regulatory evidence generation. Drawing on expertise associated with the American Statistical Association?s Cell and Gene Therapy Scientific Working Group, the workshop examines core design and analysis challenges, including single-arm and randomized trials, dose finding, historical borrowing, estimands, operational considerations, and the production of credible, publishable evidence in settings with limited samples and heterogeneous populations. The seminar also considers the growing role of artificial intelligence in cell and gene therapy development, helping participants understand how emerging computational tools may influence discovery, decision support, evidence synthesis, reproducibility, and interpretation in this fast-moving field.

Sign up today <https://instats.org//seminar/cell-and-gene-therapy-design-estimands-o> to secure your spot, and feel free to share this opportunity with colleagues and students who might benefit!


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Tidy Data, Visualisation, and AI
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Transparent preparation helps epidemiological analyses remain interpretable from data to display. Tidy Data, Visualisation, and AI is a 2-day seminar livestreaming September 21?22 with Flavio Lombardo (Institute for Statistical and Data Science). Diagnose inconsistent codes, missing-value markers, and date formats, then reshape data into tidy structures in R. Epidemiological researchers can use dplyr, tidyr, and ggplot2 to prepare analysis datasets and create clear displays for studies. The seminar also examines AI-assisted text extraction, with attention to checking and auditing its output.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/tidy-data-visualisation-and-ai
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

Cell-level evidence can add biological detail to population health research. Single Cell Data Analysis 3.0 is a seminar livestreaming October 20, led by Nikolay Oskolkov (Lund University). Quality control, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and differential expression form a practical single-cell RNA sequencing workflow. R and Python tools, including Seurat and Scanpy, support dataset integration and biological interpretation. Epidemiological researchers can apply these methods to study cellular heterogeneity in health-related research datasets.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/single-cell-data-analysis-30
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.
